News.title: Iran’s regime has been beheaded – so what’s stopping revolution? How bloodthirsty ‘final pillar’ is propping up tyranny
News.content:
DONALD Trump issued a rallying cry to Iranians to “take back their country” just hours after Ayatollah Ali Khamenei’s inglorious death.

But more than five weeks later, his regime is clinging to power thanks to its “final pillar” – the ruthless Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps.





Insiders say the bloodthirsty militants will “stop at no crime” to protect the regime by violently stamping out any hint of rebellion.

The powerful IRGC has taken de facto control of the rogue state after dozens of top leaders were wiped out.

Taking down the regime’s crucial defenders is the key to unlocking a revolution inside Iran, activists and analysts say.

A spokesman for the National Council of Resistance of Iran said: “Neither appeasement nor foreign war can put an end to the Iran crisis that has engulfed the whole region.



“The only solution to Iran crisis is regime change by the Iranian people and their organised resistance.

“The key question is: how can such a regime, one that spares no crime to preserve itself, be overthrown?

“As a result of economic and social crises, and the loss of its regional tentacles, the regime of the absolute rule of the clergy now has only one pillar of support left: the Revolutionary Guard Corps.

“So, to overthrow the clerical regime, the IRGC has to be removed.



“The Guards have shown hundreds of times, including during the January uprising, that they will stop at no crime to preserve the regime.”

Armed to the teeth, the IRGC is known to show no mercy – including during January’s deadly protests.

British-Iranian activist Haleh Blake told The Sun: “My friends are still missing since that day and every other Iranian family I know has had at least one person killed.

“The crackdown was brutal. Following that, people couldn’t come out.

“Tanks and machine guns were stationed and the forces were shooting at anyone passing for some days.”



Insiders in Iran told The Sun last month how the IRGC had again ramped up terror on the streets, with armed agents patrolling the streets and mass arrests.

Iran rebels defy internet blackout to reveal they are READY to topple regime Exclusive by Katie Davis, Deputy Foreign Editor BRAVE Iranian rebels have broken through the regime’s internet blackout to tell The Sun: “We are ready to finally take our country back”. Ayatollah Ali Khamenei’s grisly downfall that saw him wind up dead in a pile of rubble has left the rogue nation’s repressed public wanting more. One defiant Iranian told me: “The endgame feels real in a way it hasn’t before.” Donald Trump hailed the chief mullah’s pathetic demise after his compound was blitzed as “the single greatest chance for the Iranian people to take back their country”. In a rallying cry to Iran’s population, the US president urged them to seize the opportunity to put the final nail in the nation’s bloodthirsty regime. Courageous Iranians – whose identities we have concealed to protect them – say they are waiting for their moment to finally topple the regime as Khamenei’s inner circle desperately tries to cling to power. Internet blackouts have made it extremely difficult to communicate but, with limited VPN connection, they have managed to share accounts. During January’s deadly protests, when ruthless Khamenei ordered his revolutionary guards to show no mercy, critics told me they would rather die than see his regime survive. But now, almost two months on, the Supreme Leader is dead, and protesters are more certain than ever they could be on the brink of freedom. One 27-year-old rebel living in Tehran told The Sun: “Many of us believed it was possible before, but those uprisings were never meant to be the final chapter by themselves. “The regime survived by hiding behind proxies, money networks, and foreign lobbying. “Now that mask is cracking and their hand is exposed, the endgame feels real in a way it hasn’t before. “It’s a strange mix of relief and iron focus. People are glad to see operations striking terrorists – but the deeper feeling is impatience and readiness. “Everyone is waiting for the moment it becomes our turn to reclaim Iran, and people talk about it out loud now. No more whispers.” READ MORE HERE

One source in Tehran said Since the bombings began, the regime’s forces have been patrolling the streets fully armed out of sheer fear.

“They know that if even a small opening is created, the people will rise up again, and they are terrified of the masses pouring into the streets.”

But more than 2,000 high-ranking IRGC members have now been killed – leaving the force scrambling to replace its troops.

Loyal IRGC members have started deserting their posts as the regime crumbles from within.



One army personnel in Tehran said: “Since the start of the current conflict, many IRGC bases and Basij headquarters have been attacked.

“This has caused many military commanders, who belong to the IRGC, to flee and go hiding out of fear.

“Chaos has now spread to many Army barracks because many commanders are effectively absent.”

In desperation, the IRGC is calling in reinforcements – and even recruiting children as young as 12 to run checkpoints.

Fanatical Shia militias from neighbouring Iraq have been crossing into Iran in recent days to support their overstretched IRGC masters being ripped apart.



The regime has also been turning up the notches of fear in the shadow of war in a bid to deter rebellion by launching a sick execution spree to silence critics.

Security forces brutally executed at least four anti-regime activists in just 48 hours this week, according to an opposition group.

A further 15 political prisoners were sentenced to death in the same time period, the NCRI said.



The group, made up of exiled regime opponents, warned that another massacre could be coming in Iran’s prisons.

Two more rebels were taken to the gallows on Sunday at Ghezel Hesar Prison.

Mohammadamin Biglari, 19, and Shahin Vahedparast Kalour, 30, were executed after being arrested during January’s protests.

Fuelled by outrage, Iranians told The Sun how they are waiting for the right moment to rise up and put the final nail in the regime’s coffin.

Haleh added: “On February 28, Trump ordered the strikes and for Iranians the help they were promised arrived.



“On the same day, Iranians were told to stay home by crown prince Reza Pahlavi, with same messaging from US and Israel.

How Trump putting boots on ground could spark uprising Exclusive by Katie Davis, Deputy Foreign Editor DONALD Trump putting boots on the ground inside Iran could spark the final deathblow to the fanatical regime. Dozens of top brass have been wiped out since the US and Israel unleashed strikes five weeks ago, weakening the regime’s iron grip. But Trump has been warned an uprising to decapitate it once and for all will only happen if a revolution is sparked within Iran. Kurdish commander Babasheikh Hosseini gave the US president a chilling ultimatum as he said there will be no victory – unless his fighters are sent into the battlefield. Before the latest war erupted, The Sun revealed how Khamenei had built a shady web of 4,000 people around him to shield his regime from demise. And after the 12-day war last year, we reported how – despite the regime “hanging by a thread” – the West would not be able to remove fanatics from power and that it was ultimately in the hands of the population. Now after weeks of relentless blitzes depleting its resources and killing many of its most powerful players, the regime is on its heels. But Kenneth Katzman, who briefed US Congress for 31 years on Iran in his role as a Middle East Analyst, said the bloodthirsty mullahs will not yet fear being ousted. He told The Sun: “Without a ground incursion the regime does not feel it is going to be toppled. “It’s going to be defiant and as we’re seeing, it will try to keep the Strait closed.” Katzman warned without a ground offensive, it will be near-impossible that the regime – which started its barbaric reign after the Islamic Revolution in 1979 – will be overthrown. READ MORE HERE

“The attacks have been very precise, and it’s safest for people to stay indoors.

“Many of our friends who went to protest on January 8 and 9 witnessed people get killed in showers of bullets in front of them.

“They tell me they also died that day, and look forward to the final protest day to finish the job. Iranians want to finish the job.”

Haleh, co-founder of United4Mahsa, said many are waiting for the green light from self-styled crown prince Reza Pahlavi – son of Iran’s ousted final Shah – to give them the green light.



“My personal view is simple, Reza Pahlavi called the protests of January where millions in over 100 cities came out, and people are remaining home due to his instructions, also instructions of the US military,” she said.

“They are waiting for the call of action from Crown Prince Reza Pahlavi to protest again.”

But Jason Brodsky, policy director at UANI, warned any sort of revolution would not happen overnight – and will be a long, complicated process.

“There would need to be a convergence of labour and political protests and mass defections among the armed forces and security services,” he told The Sun.

“We are not at that point yet. But when the dust settles, protests could erupt again as they did months after the 12-Day War last year.

“It’s a process of regime collapse and it doesn’t happen overnight.

“The weakness of the current regime could embolden the Iranian people, especially with the erosion of the internal security apparatus.”

News.title: At least 10 people critically injured as ‘overloaded’ 60ft Ferris wheel collapses leaving dozens trapped underneath
News.content:
AT least 10 people have been critically injured after an “overloaded” Ferris wheel collapsed leaving dozens more trapped underneath.

Shocking video shows the amusement ride slowly tip sideways before completely collapsing to the ground – with riders left dangling from their seats.





The structure’s supports can be seen giving way as onlookers try to help the people trapped beneath the wreckage.

Witnesses said the wheel had completed two rotations before loud creaking noises began at the night-time fair on April 1.

It came after reported desperate warnings from onlookers to operators.

Moments later, the 60ft structure collapsed – severely injuring at least 10 people.

At least 80 people were on board at the time.

It’s understood 30 people- including women and children – were left with minor injuries.

Emergency services and bystanders rushed to help those hurt at the Bhainsaha Mela fair in India.



It reportedly took nearly an hour to free everyone trapped in the wreckage.

Local reports say ambulances transported at least 10 critically injured people to a nearby hospital.

Two children are said to be in serious condition.

Preliminary findings suggest the base of the ride was weak, poorly anchored, and unable to withstand the “excessive” load.

Authorities are probing possible negligence and safety lapses.



Horrifically, it’s not the first collapse of an amusement ride in India this year.

In February, one person died and 13 more injured when a spinning fairground ride detached from its frame mid-spin, catapulting the riders to the ground.

Chilling video footage from an onlooker shows the ride making two successful turns before separating from one of the side pillars.



The seating component of the swing continued on its upward trajectory for a few seconds before plummeting to the ground.

People were heard screaming in the background of the video as the chaos unfolded at the Surajkund International Craft Festival in Haryana, Faridabad.

The joyride in India quickly collapsed, killing a police officer in the process.

News.title: Should workers pick up tab for lifting two-child benefit cap? VOTE NOW
News.content:
POLL OF THE DAY Should workers pick up tab for lifting two-child benefit cap? VOTE NOW

WORKING families will bear the brunt of the two-child benefit cap being scrapped, the Conservative Party has warned.

Lifting the cap is expected to cost £3.4billion and will be funded by increased taxes on working households including higher council tax and utility bills.



From today, basic rate taxpayers could see their bills increase by up to £1,000 a year, while households of two unemployed adults and three children could get an extra £6,400 in benefits.



Labour said removing the two child limit on universal credit will bring 450,000 children out of poverty.

Kemi Badenoch has blasted the policy as a “benefits payday” which will “leave working families picking up the tab”.

News.title: My mum’s boyfriend had killed before – but he was still free to murder her… we still don’t know what he did with body
News.content:
FIONA Holm’s family had spent two weeks pleading with police to do more to find their missing sister – so they went to confront her older boyfriend.

And when they arrived at Carl Cooper’s flat in Catford, they found he had painted his windows all black – and they were told he had been spotted burning items in his back garden. But the revelation the devastated family made later was even more disturbing, he had killed before.



Monster killer Cooper, then 66, was eventually jailed for 35 years for the murder of Fiona and his previous partner Naomi Hunte.



But both families remain baffled as to how he was not only free to kill – but free to kill twice.

The handyman had been reported by cops by both women for his controlling behaviour – and he was on bail after being arrested for killing Naomi.

Fiona’s family only discovered he was already a suspected killer after he was arrested for her murder – and they say they should have been warned by police.

And if they had – perhaps Fiona, who was last seen on CCTV in a Bromley off licence, would still be alive.

Her body has still never been found – with the family facing a never-ending heartbreak.



Naomi was stabbed to death by Cooper in February 2022, and Fiona went missing in June 2023.

Three years on – both families feel like they have not got justice, and are demanding answers from the police.

Naomi’s dad Basil told The Sun: “This is an injustice. I feel like the police walked all over us.

“On a scale of one to ten, my faith and trust in the police is very low – minus one.”

Fiona’s younger sister Elise added: “They should have protected her. They’re not living our nightmare.”



She went on: “I know they didn’t actually put the knife in, but they could have prevented it.

I don’t know if my mum’s in the playground or in the park or fields and stuff that we take the kids to Savannah ,

Cooper was already suspected of Naomi’s murder when he entered into a relationship with Fiona, a woman whose family say was “very vulnerable” with the mental age of a teenager.

Before she went missing, she had reported Cooper to the police alleging he had hit her with a crow bar and stabbed her with a screwdriver.

Despite being under investigation, no action was taken.

Fiona’s sister Elise, 41, and daughter Savannah, 29, told The Sun how they were forced to conduct their own search for Fiona after she disappeared in 2023.



Elise said: “We used to ring them all the time. We rang them every day. Even if we heard that someone had said something, we’d ring them.”

They said they even told officers that Cooper had repainted the outside of his windows and that neighbours spotted him burning items in his back garden which made a “funny smell”.

Elise said: “They was like ‘it’s not a crime to burn rubbish’.



“The police weren’t listening to us,” Savannah added.

They later went to Cooper’s home and found that he was selling Fiona’s clothes.

Astonishingly, despite being under investigation at the time for Naomi’s murder, he wasn’t put in cuffs until July 11.

That window of time, the family fear, would have provided ample opportunity to try and discard evidence and dispose of Fiona’s body.



Savannah said: “I don’t really want to live in this area anymore because he lived in it.

“I don’t know if my mum’s in the playground or in the park or fields and stuff that we take the kids to.

“It gives you anxiety. Every time you’re going past places that you’ve searched, you’ll look again thinking ‘did I miss something?’”

Following his arrest, Fiona’s blood was founding on clothing at Cooper’s address with bloodstains detected on the walls, door and wi-fi router in his living room.

Savannah added: “If they hadn’t taken so long to actually listen to us, we could have recovered my mother’s body or found more evidence”



The police later visited Savannah’s house and told her that Carl Cooper had killed before leaving her speechless.

“We just couldn’t believe it,” she said.

“I can’t describe him. There isn’t a word in the English language. To see everything unfold in front of me [in court] made me cry Basil ,

Naomi Hunte told the Met she was terrified of Cooper before he stabbed her to death in 2022.

She had repeatedly called the police claiming Cooper was stalking her, describing him as “some sort of psychopath”.

Woolwich Crown Court heard how Naomi suffered a 12.5cm wound to the upper half of her chest that had punctured her right lung and she “would’ve died within the hour”.



Four days later, Cooper was arrested as an “obvious suspect” but denied killing Naomi and, astonishingly, released on bail.

Prosecutor, Joel Smith KC, said police had been called by Naomi’s neighbours on February 14.

He told the court that when officers entered her flat, they saw Naomi “lying across the sofa in the lounge”.



Naomi’s father, Basil, told The Sun how his only child was a “happy girl and we laughed a lot”.

He said: “We had a great relationship. She would come to see me at least twice a week and we would sit and talk about all sorts of things.

“There is now a deep void in my life. I am struggling for words to express my feelings of grief and loss.

“We are going to suffer the loss for the rest of our lives as we think about Naomi every day.

He said that it was “such a failing” that his daughter had not been protected by the police.



“There is a deep wound that will never heal,” he said.”

Basil says the police “walked over” the family – saying his trust in cops is “minus one”, and added that he blames racism for them not being taken seriously.

Basil recalls the moment he came face-to-face with his daughter’s killer in the street.

He said: “I saw the man three days after he killed my daughter on the street and his body language was telling me something because when he turned his face and he saw me, he was at a bus stop and he tried to run away and I thought ‘what’s wrong with him’?

Something radically has to be done because this cannot go on Pragna Patel ,

“I can’t describe him. There isn’t a word in the English language. To see everything unfold in front of me [in court] made me cry. “



Basil said when he later discovered Cooper had gone on to kill again, he was left “shocked and confused”.

The Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) has launched an investigation.

The police watchdog is examining a report made by Fiona against Cooper around two months before her murder which saw him arrested but not charged.

A review over the management of that complaint concluded “a more thorough investigation could have identified key witnesses, who could have provided strong evidence for a victimless prosecution against Cooper”.

Meanwhile, a call made just days after Fiona was killed that tipped off police officers that Cooper had done so was marked as a hoax which is also being investigated.



IOPC comment: IOPC director Amanda Rowe said: "Our sympathies are with the families and friends of Naomi Hunte and Fiona Holm and anyone affected by their deaths. “We can confirm, as part of our ongoing investigation into the prior contact Met Police officers had with both women before their murders, that we have now served disciplinary notices on ten Met officers in total. “From May 2025, we informed a detective sergeant and a detective constable that they were being investigated for potential gross misconduct; and informed a detective inspector and two police constables that they were being investigated for potential misconduct. “This relates to police actions following Ms Holm’s report to the Met, in April 2023, of a reported assault by her partner Carl Cooper. “Our investigation subsequently widened and, since September, we have served gross misconduct notices on three police constables and a police sergeant in relation to reports Ms Hunte had made to the Met about Cooper in April and October 2021. “In January 2026, we also served a police constable, who was working in the control centre, with a misconduct notice relating to a call about a reported murder that also mentioned Cooper in June 2023, which was marked as a hoax call. Ms Holm was reported missing several days after the call. “In July 2024, Cooper was convicted of the murder of both women. Our investigation began following referrals in October 2024 from the Met of complaints made by the families of both victims, alleging serious shortcomings in the force’s investigations prior to their deaths. “The serving of conduct notices does not necessarily mean disciplinary proceedings will follow. At the end of our investigation, we will decide whether any officers should face misconduct proceedings. “All parties have been kept informed of developments in the investigation.”

Despite Cooper being put behind bars for life with a minimum sentence of 35 years in July 2024, Elise says “Fiona hasn’t got justice”.

Savannah added: “I want them to take accountability, not just a sorry, we’re going to learn from this.”

Elise, Savannah and Basil have come together to support the Double Injustice campaign calling for the police to be held to account for failings in the investigation.

Basil said: “I am hoping that things like this never happen again. At one time, I respected the law but there have been so many failings that there are now doubts in my mind. “

Pragna Patel, co-director of the group Project Resist, which is helping with the families’ campaign said there is a “continual issue across the UK about failure to protect women”.



“This campaign is really about ensuring justice for both families,” she said.

“Something radically has to be done because this cannot go on.”

She added that this was not just down to individual shortcomings but that it was a “systemic problem”.

“When there are 10 officers, it becomes systemic and it becomes a structural issue, not a question of a few bad apples in the police force.”

Met Police Response Commander Paul Brogden, responsible for the Met’s Homicide Command, said: “Our thoughts will always remain with Naomi Hunte and Fiona Holm, and we again extend our sincere condolences to their families as they continue to grieve for these two beloved women. “We have always been clear that we made mistakes when dealing with allegations against Carl Cooper. For those mistakes we are extremely sorry. “These matters are currently the subject of an investigation by the Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC). As part of that investigation, ten officers have been served with misconduct notices. “We continue to provide every support to the IOPC investigation.”

News.title: Joanna Lumley ‘targeted by masked motorbike thugs who tried to steal her car from outside her £2.5m house in London’
News.content:
'BIKER BANDITS' Joanna Lumley ‘targeted by masked motorbike thugs who tried to steal her car from outside her £2.5m house in London’

JOANNA Lumley was allegedly targeted by masked motorbike thugs who attempted to steal her car from outside her home.

National treasure Joanna, 79, saw thieves target the motor at her South London home in Stockwell last week as a crime wave sweeps the capital.





The Absolutely Fabulous star reportedly emerged from her £2.5 million townhouse in her dressing gown to find a criminal gang on motorbikes attempting to start her car.

As the car alarm blared, Joanna and her neighbor dashed outside to scream at the thieves before they fled the scene, according to a neighbour.

Emma Duncan wrote in The Times that she had been “woken in the middle of the night by a commotion”.

She recalled: “A group of men on motorbikes had surrounded a car whose alarm was going off; one of them was sitting in the driver’s seat, yelling ‘I can’t f****** start it!”

She added that despite scaring the thieves off, the car was left with damage to the boot.

The Met Police say they have been investigating a spate of vehicle crime offences in the Vauxhall Park area of Lambeth.

Three reports of damage to vehicles in an attempt to gain entry were reported between March 26 and March 28.

The force said officers have spoken with local residents to gather intelligence and advise on vehicle crime prevention.



According to the Daily Mail, neighbours revealed a number of motors, including a 90s Rolls Royce, had been smashed into recently on Joanna Lumley’s road.

One said there had been a number of instances recently by criminals “driving on motorbikes”

A spokesperson for the Met said: “Tackling car theft and other neighbourhood crime remains a priority for the Met.

“We have strengthened neighbourhood policing, with more officers focused on identifying and targeting the most prolific offenders who cause the greatest harm to communities.

“Across London, vehicle crime, including theft and damage to vehicles, is down by almost 15 per cent compared with this time last year.”



The Sun has contacted Lumley’s representatives for comment.

Elsewhere in South London, this is the moment a driver rams a machete-wielding “thief” as he reportedly attempted to steal a motorbike.

Footage shows the motorist using his Land Rover to tackle the suspected crook outside a Sainsbury’s in Brixton, South London.

Last week, gangs of marauding teens sparked chaos in Clapham as Sadiq Khan was accused of failing to get a grip on crime in the capital.

The brazen mobs caused chaos in Clapham High Street twice in a matter of days, after similar scenes were seen in Birmingham last Saturday.



Shops including Waitrose, Sainsbury’s and McDonald’s were forced to close early as cops fought to bring the chaotic situation under control.

Retail bosses have slammed London’s Mayor for failing to tackle crime following the mayhem.

M&S chiefs have written to Mr Khan and Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood as the offences in their stores become “more routine”.

The Sun reported last week how thousands of prolific shoplifters could escape prison under Labour’s new plan to eliminate most jail sentences of less than a year.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Stores are bracing for further disorder, with a leading supermarket boss calling for security staff to be equipped with pepper spray and batons.



The Metropolitan Police vowed more arrests would be made after the unrest while Mayor of London, Sadiq Khan, said the “scenes we saw in Clapham earlier this week were utterly unacceptable”.

News.title: Wolf bites boy, 1, after tot stuck his hand into enclosure after sneaking past no-go zone as ‘parents sat on phones’
News.content:
A ONE-YEAR-OLD child has been bitten by a wolf after sneaking into a restricted area and sticking his hand into its enclosure.

Parents of the tot were allegedly distracted by their phones when the boy managed to crawl away and tried to touch a wolf that snapped at his hand.





The chaos led to a spokesperson for ZooAmerica saying that the wolf acted in a friendly manner and didn’t intend to cause any harm.

They said the wolf “briefly” held the child’s hand in its mouth in an “investigatory” manner before letting go.

A spokesperson added: “Wolves investigate, test, and interact with unfamiliar objects through ‘mouthing,’ which can include gently taking something into the mouth without intent to injure.”

Park staff believe the unsupervised 17-month-old child crawled under a perimeter fence and made his way towards a second metal barrier surrounding the wolves’ habitat.

He was only pulled to safety by shocked bystanders who claimed to see the boy being pulled towards the fence by the caged animal.

Parents Carrie Sortor, 43, and Stephen Wilson, 61, were allegedly looking at their phones at the time, Derry Township police told WGAL.

The pair were sitting on a bench just 25ft away when the wounded boy was escorted back to them.

Sortor and Wilson have since both been charged with a first-degree misdemeanour count of endangering the welfare of children.



The boy suffered minor injuries and went home safely after receiving medical attention at the park.

ZooAmerica said in a statement: “Our habitats are designed with multiple layers of protection, and clear signage and barriers are in place to help ensure safe viewing.

“Guests are expected to remain within designated areas and closely supervise children at all times.”

They also assured guests that the animals are not aggressive at the zoo as they told USA TODAY: “This type of response is consistent with natural animal behavior.”

Three grey wolves are housed at the 11-acre park which has over 200 various types of animals.



They include Twister, a male wolf, and two sisters in Hazel and Freya.

It is unclear which animal interacted with the boy.

ZooAmerica sits within the major tourist attraction of Hersheypark 100 miles west of Philadelphia.

It comes just days after a woman was attacked by a wolf outside an Ikea in Germany.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The wild beast mauled the woman’s face while she was trying to lead it away from other shoppers in Hamburg.



She was left bleeding after suffering a wound at the corner of her mouth and cheek which required stitches.

News.title: Hero policewoman who saved toddler’s life on beach avoids sack after ‘groping’ man on drunken night out
News.content:
COP SHOCK Hero policewoman who saved toddler’s life on beach avoids sack after ‘groping’ man on drunken night out

A POLICEWOMAN has avoided the sack after groping a man on a boozy night out with pals.

PC Zoe Williams, who previously received a bravery award for saving a toddler’s life, was found to have committed “gross misconduct”.





A police misconduct hearing heard how Williams allegedly assaulted a man in the RAFA Club in St Davids, Pembrokeshire in August 2024.

The man alleged that the police officer had “touched or cupped his groin” without his consent while she was drunk.

CCTV footage revealed Williams was “quite disinhibited” and was “dancing in a fairly extravagant manner” at the club.

The panel heard how her group of pals had met a group of men on the way to the club after consuming “a significant number of alcoholic drinks“.



She told the hearing how she had consumed four or five double G&Ts as well as several Baby Guinesses at the pub, followed by a shot of Sambuca at the club.

The off-duty copper then approached one of the men who she was “particularly interested” in.

At the hearing, the panel concluded that Williams had deliberately committed “a brief, isolated incident of sexual touching”.

It added: “The Panel finds that the misconduct in this case is so serious that it could result in the dismissal of the officer and is assessed as being gross misconduct.”



Williams appeared at the hearing and “vehemently denied the allegation against her”.

She claimed that she had accidentally touched the man when brushing past him in the club.

“I do not know his name. I was moving past him and instinctively moved him by touching his midriff. There was no assault,” Williams insisted.

She told the panel that she had not fancied the man or wanted something to happen between them.

While the panel found that she had committed gross misconduct, the disgraced officer was allowed to keep her job and handed a final written warning.



It said: “To dismiss PC Williams would be disproportionately harsh towards her and would harm the community where she lives and works by depriving it of someone who has proved to be a good police officer in the past.

“In the Panel’s judgement this was an isolated incident which was out

of character for PC Williams.”

PC Williams joined Dyfed Powys Police in July 2020.

She was spared a sacking in large part because of her heroic actions to save the life of a toddler in January 2024.

While off-duty and walking her dog on Solva Harbour Beach, Williams came to the aid of a screaming mother.



The two-year-old child had collapsed and was unresponsive.

Williams took control of the situation, administering CPR until medical help arrived.

“The child was saved and made a full recovery. This was principally due to the efforts of PC Williams.”

She was awarded commendations from the Chief Constable of Dyfed Powys Police and the High Sheriff of Dyfed for her brave action to save the child’s life.

Other written testimony from colleagues characterised her as a diligent and compassionate officer.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

The man she allegedly groped had not made a complaint at the time or later.

Ultimately, Williams was handed a 2 year final written warning to make it clear her behaviour had been inappropriate.

News.title: Dramatic moment plane suddenly makes emergency landing narrowly dodging confused drivers on busy road
News.content:
THIS is the dramatic moment a plane makes a sudden emergency landing on a motorway as the brave pilot dodges confused drivers.

Morning commuters got a shock when the small aircraft touched down on the busy dual-carriage road on Saturday morning.





Dashcam footage captured the incredible moment the pilot navigated the tricky landing – using Interstate 78 in Pennsylvania as a makeshift runway.

The plane suddenly started experiencing engine trouble not long after departing Solberg, New Jersey, en route to Indiana.

The Michigan pilot, 65, reportedly didn’t want to land on the highway but realised he had no choice to save himself and his passenger.

A witness said the pilot looked calm despite the high-stakes landing.

“He landed in two lanes. His wings were literally from almost the centre median to the grass on the other side,” the witness said.

“He didn’t look like he was freaking out, he was just looking straight ahead.”

Neither the pilot, nor the passenger, 34, were injured.

Weisenberg Volunteer Fire Chief Justin Oswald said: “This is probably the best possible outcome for this type of incident we could see.”



“It’s one of those things that you don’t necessarily train for. You don’t anticipate an aircraft landing on your highway.

“Everybody worked together very well to do something we don’t run into every day.”

Crews helped tow the plane to an airport in nearby Allentown for repairs.

The eastbound lanes of I-78 fully reopened by 1 pm.

The Federal Aviation Administration is investigating the incident.

News.title: I feel transformed after losing 10 stone - I ignore people who say I took easy way out
News.content:
I feel transformed after losing 10 stone - I ignore people who say I took easy way out

Becka says people used to yell insults at her in the street

View 6 Images (Image: Jam Press/@beckalosesit)

A teacher who endured abuse in the street has finally found confidence in her own skin after dropping more than 10 stone. Becka Gill used to avoid mirrors and pull out of plans because she felt so mortified by her appearance - but now feels 'transformed'.

‌



The 34 year old tipped the scales at 19st 3lbs and wore a size 24. Now a size eight after losing 10st 2lbs over three years, Becka says she can finally face her reflection with a smile.

‌



"Before my weight loss, I was in an extremely low place," Becka, from Congleton, Cheshire, told creatorzine.com. "I would sob in the shower because I didn't even want to touch my own body.

‌



View 6 Images (Image: Jam Press/@beckalosesit)

"I cancelled any social life because I never felt comfortable in anything I wore or couldn't find anything to wear. I felt self conscious anywhere I went and I had a fear of eating in public because I wondered what people would think of a big girl eating food.

"It meant I wasn't able to date because I didn't like myself. And I've been called fat in public by men and shamed for the way I looked.

‌



"On a night out, a man told me I was fat and told his mate to come away from me. I didn't respond but it cut deep."

View 6 Images (Image: Jam Press/@beckalosesit)

Becka splashed out £3,000 on a gastric sleeve procedure in Turkey in July 2022, which helped her shed six stone. Following the operation, she regained a stone, leaving her feeling frustrated and concerned she would never achieve a place of comfort in her own body.

‌



Determined not to surrender, she began using Mounjaro in January 2025 while making sustainable lifestyle modifications. Becka said she has encountered criticism online for her surgery and for using the injections.

She said: "My family and friends have always been incredibly supportive of the choices I've made to lose weight. Obviously, both options I've taken are controversial to some.

View 6 Images Becka has transformed her appearance (Image: Jam Press/@beckalosesit)

‌



"I've had a lot of comments online - mostly supported but there's always the trolls out there that want to put you down or want to put their opinion across. People are quick to tell me I've taken the easy way out but, again, unless you've actually been through this journey you don't actually realise how difficult it actually is and how much work you have to put in if you're doing it properly."

Now at a weight she describes as "comfortable", Becka is concentrating on toning up and exercising to achieve the appearance she desires. However, she maintains the biggest transformation has been internal.

She said: "I'm finally at a point in my journey where I feel truly comfortable in my own skin. For the first time, I smile at the person looking back at me in the mirror.

‌



View 6 Images Becka now feels 'truly comfortable' (Image: Jam Press/@beckalosesit)

"I still don't really believe I can order clothes and have them fit perfectly when they arrive. No sending things back, no second-guessing sizes.

"It feels surreal. But more than that, it feels right. I finally feel like the real me, the version of myself I've always wanted to be.

‌



"And it's changed so much more than just how I look. It's transformed how I feel. I'm happier. I'm living life the way I've always imagined.

View 6 Images Becka says she is a lot happier now (Image: Jam Press/@beckalosesit)

"I find joy in the smallest things now. I laugh more and I romanticise everyday moments. I even enjoy going to the gym.

Article continues below

"It took time to rebuild the confidence to walk back through those doors but now I genuinely look forward to working out. Exercise isn't something I dread anymore, it's something that makes me feel strong, capable, and proud.

"For the first time in a long time, I feel like me."

News.title: 'My restaurants are loved by royals - Queen Camilla showed true colours during visit'
News.content:
'My restaurants are loved by royals - Queen Camilla showed true colours during visit'

Having welcomed Princess Diana, King Charles, and Queen Camilla to his restaurants, Jeremy King shared what it has been like to host such iconic figures

View 3 Images Queen Camilla didn't want to attract attention, according to Jeremy

Restaurateur Jeremy King has welcomed a series of famous faces over the years at his eateries — including royalty such as Princess Diana and Queen Camilla. Reflecting on hosting the current Queen, Jeremy shared why her personality away from the cameras fills him with admiration.

‌



He told Hello! Magazine: "There are some people who want to be seen and some who are entirely natural. All I can say is that the Queen is entirely natural.

‌



"She falls into the category of somebody who just wants to be with their guests and not attract attention. There are the people I admire the most."

‌



Once dubbed the place to be in the eighties, Jeremy's bistro Le Caprice attracted a star-studded clientele, including Sir Elton John and Dame Joan Collins.

The restaurant was also beloved by Princess Diana, who frequented it regularly before her death in 1997.

According to the publication, such famous faces were drawn to his restaurant because they embraced the normality away from the fame - Diana included.

‌



View 3 Images Princess Diana often dined at Jeremy's Le Caprice

He recalled: "When the Princess of Wales started frequenting the restaurant [in the mid-eighties], she'd walk through the door and very quickly get noticed. There'd be a lot of, 'Don't look now, but it's the Princess of Wales.'

"People would see her sit down, then they would look at the restaurant to see what the reaction was."

‌



Jeremy continued: "They'd expect me to go running over to the table like Uriah Heep, wringing my hands."

But according to the restaurateur, Diana didn't expect such treatment despite her high-profile status.

"She didn't want that. I'd go and talk to the least-known person in the place," he added. "I think she thought that I offered sanctuary."

‌



Recalling a particular moment, he said Diana was such a regular visitor that they often organised joint outings for his staff and hers at Kensington Palace, including one occasion go-karting in Croydon.

View 3 Images Restaurateur Jeremy King has welcomed a series of famous faces over the years at his eateries

"She encouraged me [to take part] because she wanted to beat me, but I declined," he remembered.

‌



Speaking further about the bond they formed, he said that while they weren't close friends, she would "talk" and "sometimes confide" in him.

According to the publication, King Charles is also a fan of his restaurant, Simpson's, based in Strand. The restaurant shut its doors during the Covid-19 pandemic but has since reopened.

Meanwhile, BBC Radio 2 presenter Sara Cox also recently opened up about an awkward blunder while meeting the Queen.

Article continues below

She told The Observer: "Yes, she's a laugh. I met her at a celebration for authors that she had at Clarence House.

"I mistook her daughter, Laura (Lopes), for an author that I half knew, and so I said to Laura, 'Come over. I'll introduce you to the duchess. Let's go over and say hi'.

"Laura played along, so we went over, and it slowly dawned on me who she was, because Camilla was like 'Hiiii' to her own daughter. It came as no surprise at all that Camilla and Jilly Cooper got on really well. I can see them as real kindred spirits," she added.

News.title: Iran embassies troll Trump with responses to unhinged Truth Social threat
News.content:
Iran embassies troll Trump with responses to unhinged Truth Social threat

Trump has been mercilessly teased by Iranian embassies around the world in a series of wildly different responses to his now infamous 'praise Allah' social media post

View 4 Images The US president has been roundly mocked by Iranian representatives

Donald Trump has been relentlessly mocked by Iranian embassies in trolling responses to his unhinged threat posted on Truth Social this weekend.

‌



The social media-obsessed leader of the world's most powerful nation declared "praise be to Allah" in a bizarre, expletive-laden Easter Sunday post promising to bomb civilian infrastructure in Iran if the nation's leaders refused to reopen the Strait of Hormuz shipping artery. Despite the foreful and increasingly desperate seeming nature of the post, in which he called his Iranian counterparts "crazy b****rds" Trump's Iranian counterparts appear unfazed.

‌



The nation has struck back with its own meme-filled posts poking fun at the angry president via its embassies in Europe, Asia and beyond.

‌



View 4 Images Trump said 'praise be to Allah' in the expletive-laden post (Image: @realDonaldTrump/X)

Donald Trump announces TWO key targets in expletive-filled rant against Iran READ MORE :

Posting a screenshot of the president's "Truth" on X, formerly Twitter, the Iranian embassy in the UK included a quote from famed American writer Mark Twain insulting his intelligence. The quote read: "It is better to keep your mouth closed and let people think you are a fool than to open it and remove all doubt ."

Iran's embassy in India responded along a similar line, saying: "Swearing and throwing insults are how sore loser brats behave. Get a grip on yourself, old man." The embassy of Bulgaria had a shorter statement, telling Trump: "Take it easy, tiger! Keep your cool."

‌



Several posts made use of generative AI, with one picture mock up posted by the Turkish embassy picturing Donald Trump and Pete Hegseth smashing a bridge down while armed with mallets. In another mocking the president's 48 hour warning, the Iranian embassy in Indonesia posted an image of Trump with a 48 hour timer paired with Iran's national flag with a loading bar saying: "Loading… since 3000 years ago" and a winking emoji.

View 4 Images The Iran embassy in Turkey posted a cartoon of Trump and Hegseth destroying a bridge (Image: @Iran_in_Turkiye/X)

‌



A different set of posts called for Trump's removal from office and accused him of crimes, with the Iranian embassy in South Africa referencing the impeachment clause in the US Constitution, stating: "Seriously think about the 25th amendment, Section 4."

Zimbabwe's Iranian embassy pointed to Trump's behaviour posting a definition of presidential decorum, saying is "refers to the expected standards of behaviour, conduct, and communication for a president while in office." It goes on to outline what it includes with a screenshot of Trump's expletive-laden Truth Social post:

"Respectful and measured language in public statements

"DIgnified behaviour that reflects the seriousness of the office

"Adherence to norms and traditions of governance

"Composure under pressure, especially during crises

"Respect for institutions, laws, and other branches of government".

‌



View 4 Images The US army has been bombing civilian infrastructure in Iran (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

In a more straight-laced statement, the Iranian embassy in Austria claimed in its post that "attacking civilian infrastructure such as bridges and power plants constitutes a war crime". The posts from Iranian embassies around the world reflect the regime's subbornness in the face of Trump's threats, with Iran similarly threatening to increase the strength of its response to US aggression.

Article continues below

General Ali Abdollahi Aliabadi, from Iran's central military command, said the threat issued by Trump was a "helpless, nervous, unbalanced and stupid action".

He pledged, similarly to the US president, that the "gates of hell will open" for him, while Mahdi Tabatabaei, a spokesman for Iran's president's office, laid down the conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz. He said it would only do so when "a portion of transit tolls is used to compensate for all the damage caused" by the war.

News.title: Putin humiliated as prized warship 'attacked by Ukraine in Russian port'
News.content:
Putin humiliated as prized warship 'attacked by Ukraine in Russian port'

A drone struck Vladimir Putin's frigate Admiral Grigorovich in the Black Sea port, according to Kyiv's drone forces commander Robert Brovdi

View Image The Admiral Grigorovich frigate is the lead ship of the Admiral Grigorovich-class frigates in the Russian Navy (Image: UAF SBS / east2west news)

A drone is believed to have struck Vladimir Putin's lead frigate Admiral Grigorovich in the Black Sea port in a fresh blow to the Russian leader.

‌



The vessel, which has been used to pummel Ukraine with deadly Kalibr cruise missiles, was hit in Novorossiysk port, according to Kyiv's drone forces commander Robert Brovdi, known by his call sign Madyar.

‌



The attack came as other targets including the oil exporting port were hit in Novorossiysk - a vital foreign currency earner for Putin’s war machine. Footage shows a drone approaching the missile-carrying Admiral Grigorovich, but it cuts out before the moment of impact.

‌



There is no independent confirmation so far of a hit but even the arrival of a Ukrainian drone so close to a prestige Russian warship is embarrassing for Putin and his air defences.

“Air defence missiles were launched from the ship during the attack, but this did not prevent the ship from hitting its target,” said a statement. "The extent of the damage is currently being determined."

Article continues below

Reports say the Russian-controlled floating drilling rig Sivash was also struck by the Ukrainian navy.

The operation was "carried out by the Birds of the 1st Unmanned Systems Forces Centre", the statement said.

The attack was planned and coordinated by the SBU, Ukraine’s security service.

News.title: City centre street 'going from bad to worse' as empty shops and delivery bikes take over
News.content:
City centre street 'going from bad to worse' as empty shops and delivery bikes take over

A restaurant owner is the 'last man standing' in this 'zombie quarter'.

View 3 Images This restaurant has thousands of glowing reviews online for its food but its owner says its future in a city centre's 'zombie quarter' is uncertain (Image: Kirsty Bosley)

A restaurant owner who says he has spent 12 years battling to keep his business afloat in the centre of Britain's second largest city says where he works is a "dead area" dominated by empty shops.

‌



Erminio Shahmani opened La Galleria on Ethel Street in Birmingham in 2014 and since then claims the neighbourhood has gone from "bad to worse" as businesses close and delivery cyclists congregate in his doorway. La Galleria is the last surviving restaurant in a corner building that was formerly a Masonic Hall and then a cinema. The restaurant is a stone's throw from Birmingham's New Street Station, one of the country's biggest and busiest rail stations, and has thousands of glowing reviews on Google and TripAdvisor for its food but finds itself in what is being called the city's 'Zombie Quarter' because of its lack of life.

‌



Erminio has worked tirelessly to make his Italian eatery a success, despite an uncertain future in the building that still harbours a poignant time capsule, reports Birmingham Live. He serves Sicilian dishes alongside plates from across Italy, with a pizza oven next to the open kitchen for freshly baked bread and slices.

‌



"My staff are from all over Italy and the chefs are too," he told Birmingham Live. "It's a proper, authentic Italian restaurant. Everything is cooked here, you order and it's all cooked fresh, you can see. Every night I have three chefs, a pizza chef and a porter as well as my waiting team. It's a real authentic Italian restaurant."

View 3 Images Restaurant owner Erminio with his staff (Image: Birmingham Live)

But who else turns up at La Galleria's doorstep each evening? Cyclists waiting for takeaway deliveries from other units along New Street.

‌



"Unfortunately the changes we've seen have been from bad to worse," Erminio said. "It used to be a very vibrant road, we had no problems, nothing to worry about. And I'm sorry to say that. You can see now, all the shops are empty, I'm the only one standing and I'll be here as long as I can."

Planning permission was granted in 2024 to transform the old building housing his restaurant into a new office and retail spot., meaning there is a cloud of uncertainty hanging over his business: "If you know you're going to be evicted from your house, you don't want to be in that house any more. But a house and a restaurant are two different things."

He added: "We're the forgotten one. This part of Birmingham should be the best part of Birmingham but it's the worst part. We've got to remain positive. If you want to move forward you can't let any of those things affect your mindset, but the reality is that the empty shops speak for themselves."

‌



View 3 Images La Galleria is among the last businesses standing in this part of the city centre (Image: Kirsty Bosley)

Colliers, the management company responsible for the building housing La Galleria, declined to comment when approached regarding the vacant units.

"Birmingham City Council should do a little bit more to help us in that respect," Erminio said.

Article continues below

"In other areas, the shops are full but this area is like a warzone. It's a dead area. We have beggars, bikers down here. They're a nightmare. I sympathise with them earning a living, I'm a foreigner in this country even though I've been here for 30 years and I've had three children.

"But they don't seem to realise that you can't sit on someone's doorstep 24/7. Even though they're harmless, they're working hard to earn a living, but it can feel intimidating when you walk past. They can be extremely inconsiderate."

News.title: Artemis 2 crew face communications blackout as astronaut says 'let's pray'
News.content:
Artemis 2 crew face communications blackout as astronaut says 'let's pray'

The blackout comes as the Artemis 2 crew prepare to pass behind the Moon today, with astronauts using the silence as an opportunity to pray they'll 'get back in contact' with mission control

View 3 Images Artemis 2 astronauts will be passing behind the Moon today (Image: NASA via Getty Images)

The Artemis 2 mission is facing a communications blackout with astronauts planning to pray as their spacecraft loses it's connection with ground control for 40 minutes.

‌



The blackout will occur as astronauts pass behind the Moon at around 23:47pm UK time (18:47pm EDT) today. It will be the first time the crew will lose contact with mission control in Houston, Texas, since their journey began on April 1.

‌



This is because radio and laser signals that keep the team in constant back-and-forth communication with Earth will be blocked by the Moon itself.

‌



Artemis pilot Victor Glover says the team will use the silence as an opportunity to come together and pray that they'll "get back in contact with the crew".

View 3 Images Artemis 2 astronauts will lose connection with mission control today (Image: AP)

"When we're behind the Moon, out of contact with everybody, let's take that as an opportunity," he told the BBC. "Let's pray, hope, send your good thoughts and feelings that we get back in contact with the crew."

‌



Those on Earth working to maintain contact with the spacecraft say they'll be "slightly nervous" as communication briefly stops. The Goonhilly Earth Station in Cornwall has been collecting signals from the Orion capsule and feeding information back to Nasa HQ.

Chief technology officer Matt Cosby said it will be the first time the team are tracking a spacecraft with humans on it.

"We're going to get slightly nervous as it goes behind the Moon, and then we'll be very excited when we see it again, because we know that they're all safe," he told the BBC.

‌



View 3 Images Mission control monitoring the Orion spacecraft (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

"For a sustainable presence on the Moon, you need the full comms - you need the full 24 hours a day, even on the far side, because the far side will want to be explored as well," he said.

The Artemis 2 mission marks the first human journey to lunar orbit since Apollo 17 in December 1972. At the time, astronauts were also left in total darkness when the signal was cut as they moved across the Moon.

Article continues below

NASA's historic Apollo 11 mission saw Michael Collins lose contact with Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin, as well as mission control, for 48 minutes as took the two astronauts took their first steps the lunar surface.

In his 1974 memoir Carrying the Fire, Collins said he felt "truly alone" and "isolated from any known life" at the time, but added that he didn't feel scared or lonely. He later said the silence offered a break from the continuous requests from mission control.

News.title: Anti-corruption cop in UK Epstein files probe vows 'relentless pursuit for justice'
News.content:
Anti-corruption cop in UK Epstein files probe vows 'relentless pursuit for justice'

Det Supt Simon Hurst, Head of Greater Manchester Police's Anti-Corruption Unit, is coordinating a national review of documents relating to paedophile financier Jeffrey Epstein

View 4 Images A UK task force has been set up to probe files relating to paedophile financier Jeffrey Epstein (Image: Corbis via Getty Images)

A senior anti-corruption cop reviewing the Epstein files has vowed to be "relentless in the pursuit for truth and justice".

Detective Superintendent Simon Hurst, Head of Greater Manchester Police's Anti-Corruption Unit, is overseeing a national review of documents which sparked a wave of criminal probes across the UK. Det Supt Hurst was assigned PIP4 status for the review - giving him the powers to focus on "the strategic management of the highly complex, high-profile, or major crime investigations".

He is working across a new national specialist team set up to identify UK violence against women identified in the released files on the US child-trafficker. But he is also focused on all other potential crimes which may emerge in the tranche of documents made public by by the US Department of Justice last month.

View 4 Images Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor was stripped of his Royal titles over his relationship with Epstein (Image: Getty)

Andrew dragged back into Epstein scandal as Hollywood drama threatens to rip open past READ MORE :

Now, writing on LinkedIn, St Supt Hurst said: "It is an honour and a privilege to be asked to help co-ordinate such important work. I promise that I, and all those that work with me, will be relentless in the pursuit for truth and justice."

Paedophile financier Epstein had links to the UK through the former Duke of York, Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor, 66, and his ex-wife Sarah Ferguson, 66. He was also linked to Labour grandee Peter Mandelson, 72, and is believed to have visited Buckingham Palace. Mandelson and Andrew have denied any wrongdoing in relation to Epstein. Epstein died in prison in 2019 aged 66 after being found hanged in his cell while awaiting trial for child trafficking offences.

Around a dozen police forces in the UK have already confirmed they are looking into any potential crimes carried out on their patch linked to Epstein. The national group set up in February to support police forces with their investigations confirmed last week it had created a separate strand to focus solely on violence against women and girls allegations.

They have already approached potential victims to share their accounts, including women who have previously spoken to BBC Newsnight and Good Morning Britain. The group is chaired by Assistant Chief Constable Claire Bell, deputy director at the National Centre for Violence Against Women and Girls and Public Protection (NCVPP).

View 4 Images Peter Mandelson - pictured with Jeffrey Epstein - has faced scrutiny over his relationship with the paedophile financier (Image: US Committee on Oversight and Government Reform)

It will prioritise identifying the scale, scope and nature of any potential UK-based offending within the files, and "establishing a nationally coordinated and consistent approach to gathering and assessing intelligence". Assistant Chief Constable Bell said last week: "Policing operates locally but must remain nationally coherent, which is why the coordination groups have been established to ensure we are joining the dots as the public would expect.

"Working with the NCA (National Crime Agency), we are reviewing and assessing the published files. We have also reached out to survivors who have shared their experiences with the media to invite them to speak to UK authorities should they feel comfortable to do so. Police forces may receive direct contact from potential victims and survivors reporting matters that are not contained in the Epstein files released. Officers will listen with care to anyone who takes the courageous step of contacting us."

View 4 Images Mandelson previously said he regretted ever meeting Epstein (Image: AP)

She said police would be "meticulous" in its assessment of the files, which include more than 3 million documents and pictures released in tranches by the US. She said: "The volume of material is significant, and the detailed assessment of the files will take time, which I fully appreciate can be both frustrating and traumatic for anyone impacted.

"But it is crucial that we get this right – taking a methodical and coordinated approach to safeguard the integrity of any potential investigations. Our priority throughout will remain the safety, wellbeing and confidence of victims."

The VAWG coordination group will work alongside the NCA and the Tackling Organised Exploitation Programme (TOEX), and draw upon the expertise of colleagues from Hydrant, the CSE (child sexual exploitation) Taskforce and Operation Beaconport. Ass Chief Const Bell added: "No single crime takes priority over another, and the establishment of this second group, and investment in additional intelligence resources reflects the increasing complexity and sensitivity of these matters.

Article continues below

"Running in tandem, the groups will enable us to consider any and all potential offending and reaffirm our commitment to victims and survivors of abuse. We remain focused on protecting people and maintaining public confidence."

US lawmakers have repeatedly called for Mr Mountbatten-Windsor to answer questions about his links to Epstein. He has denied any wrongdoing over his Epstein links. Pressure is also mounting on Ms Ferguson to testify in the US over her apparent friendship with Epstein, although there has been no formal request for her to do so.

Files released by the Department of Justice in January revealed she remained in contact with the disgraced financier, including just 17 days before his release from a Florida jail for soliciting sex with minors. Last month both Mr Mandelson and Mr Mountbatten-Windsor were separately arrested by police in connection with the passing of information to Epstein. They were both released under investigation.

News.title: William and Kate's non-negotiable move after Andrew scandal - 'they'll feel justified'
News.content:
EXCLUSIVE: William and Kate's non-negotiable move after Andrew scandal - 'they'll feel justified'

The Prince and Princess of Wales are set to take a short break from royal duties as they enjoy the Easter holidays with their children Prince George, Princess Charlotte and Prince Louis

View 7 Images The Prince and Princess of Wales with their children on Easter Sunday (Image: PA)

The Easter holidays are in full swing - and now taking a break from their royal duties are the Prince and Princess of Wales.

‌



The couple nearly always block out their schedules when their children Prince George, Princess Charlotte and Prince Louis are on their school holidays so they can spend quality time together. The Easter break comes after a much busier start to 2026 compared to the previous year, with both William and Kate travelling up and down the country for engagements - and in the prince's case, a trip to Saudi Arabia too.

‌



There's been state visits at Windsor Castle, attending the installation of the new Archbishop of Canterbury, outings in both Lon don and Wales, all while being forced to navigate the Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor crisis.

‌



View 7 Images Kate walks to church with George, Charlotte and Louis (Image: PA)

Royal Family's newest members join William and Kate for debut at Easter service READ MORE :

The couple also brought their children to the royal's annual Easter Sunday service at Windsor Castle yesterday, joining the royals for the ceremony for the first time since 2023. But as royal expert Jennie Bond exclusively tells the Mirror, all this is will now be put aside for a few weeks so they can fulfill their other important role - being parents to their three children and enjoying precious time together.

‌



The former BBC royal correspondent explained: "Both William and Catherine have put in quite a shift in recent weeks and months. They’ve been out and about, up and down the country. So I think they’ll feel justified in taking as much time as they can over the Easter holidays to be with their children. I know people say 'Well, I work hard too, but I don’t get to ring-fence the school holidays'.

View 7 Images Charlotte smiles at dad William (Image: PA)

"But the fact is that William and Catherine have a job for life: there is no retirement age for a King and Queen. So I don’t begrudge them taking this valuable time to be with their young children as much as they can. Their holiday plans are always private, but the chances are they will spend most of their time at their home in Norfolk, Anmer Hall.

‌



"I’m sure they’ll welcome the chance to get away from the scandal surrounding William’s disgraced uncle, Andrew – who, of course, is now living just a few miles from Anmer Hall. Meanwhile, the children will always enjoy having their granny and grandad around, and the Middletons are also very easy and welcome company for William and Catherine, who adore them."

View 7 Images Kate with oldest child Prince George, who turns 13 in July (Image: Samir Hussein./WireImage)

Of course for William and Kate, keeping three energetic children of differing ages and with differing interests may not be easy. But it seems the couple have managed to strike a balance with their 'holiday rules' focusing on the likes of outdoor activities, getting their hands dirty and being with their two beloved cocker spaniels, Orla and their new puppy - while school work is temporarily cast aside.

‌



Jennie added: "William and Kate are sure to be encouraging their children to enjoy all the outdoor activities they love as a family: romps on the beach, long walks with the dogs, barbecues if the weather is good enough and all sorts of sports.

"Especially after her cancer diagnosis, the princess relishes every moment she can spend outdoors – no matter what the weather. And she has always encouraged her children to do the same. They love the wide open spaces in Norfolk, the freedom they have to explore the Sandringham estate and also to play, pretty unhindered, on the beaches.

“It must be so liberating for them to be able to leap over the sand dunes or walk the dogs, almost like any other family. The Sandringham farm also offers an opportunity for all sorts of fun for the children, tractors to watch, animals to feed and fruit to pick.

‌



View 7 Images The Wales children are currently on their Easter holidays from school (Image: @KensingtonRoyal/Josh Shinner)

"I wouldn’t be in the least surprised if the children were given a few household chores such as tidying their rooms, filling the dishwasher, brushing the dog and cleaning up after the puppies.

"William and Catherine have both lived life outside the Palace walls, shopping, cooking and cleaning when they were at university and, afterwards, when they lived on Anglesey. They will want their children to understand that, even if you’re royal, you can still treat your home and parents with respect - and pull your weight."

‌



However, one strict holiday rule George, Charlotte and Louis will also seemingly have to abide by is a limited amount of screentime. Like parents everywhere, William and Kate are having to raise their children in a new digital world - and in recent months, both have been vocal about their wariness when it comes to smartphones and other devices.

Last October, Kate publicly flagged her caution about the problems posed by modern technology at the expense of family life in an essay written in collaboration with Professor Robert Waldinger, director of the Harvard Study of Adult Development. The princess, who took the lead in the article, said that focusing on good connections with family and friends was the key to a healthy and happy life.

View 7 Images Kate with her three children George, Charlotte and Louis (Image: PA)

‌



The essay read: “When we check our phones during conversations, scroll through social media during family dinners, or respond to e-mails while playing with our children, we’re not just being distracted, we are withdrawing the basic form of love that human connection requires.

“The challenge is particularly acute for today’s babies and young children who have been born into a world immersed in digital technology."

Meanwhile, in an interview during a trip to Brazil for his glittering Earthshot Prize Awards, Willliam too spoke out about how they don't allow their children to have smartphones, saying: “‘I think children can access too much stuff they don’t need to see online.”

‌



View 7 Images William and Kate will be taking a short break from duties (Image: PA)

But he admitted it had become a tricky situation, especially with 12-year-old George. And Jennie added: "We know there’s a bit of tension over George wanting a smartphone and also about screen time, but, like a growing number of parents, William and Catherine seem determined to hold the line on this for as long as they can. The compromise will probably turn out to be a 'brick phone' without access to social media."

It comes as the Easter holidays will mark somewhat of a turning point for George, who officially turns a teenager in July when he celebrates his 13th birthday. When he returns to Lambrook School after the break, he will be in his final term at the school before heading off to secondary education in September.

‌



At some point in the coming months, it is expected that William and Kate will announce which school George will start at when the new school year commences in September. Both Eton and Marlborough College, his parents’ former schools, are said to be frontrunners.

But for Jennie, she believes William and Kate will continue to encourage all of their children to get involved family-focused time, even if it means adapting their current plans in future years as their children get older - and becoming even more adventurous.

Temperatures are set to surge as high as 24C in London later this week, making the capital hotter than Barcelona, according to the Met Office.

The blustery conditions of Storm Dave are forecast to be replaced by sunshine and warm weather with temperatures set to reach 24C in London and 20C in Manchester on Wednesday.

Highs of 24C would be enough to surpass the hottest day of the year so far, which was 20.9C in Gogerddan near Aberystwyth on 18 March.

It will also mean many parts of the UK will be hotter than Barcelona which is set to reach 19C on Tuesday and Wednesday this week.

Tuesday will also be sunny in the UK with temperatures reaching 20C in London and 19C in Glasgow.

London could see highs of 24C on Wednesday, according to the Met Office ( Met Office )

However the warm weather is not set to last as the Met Office has forecast temperatures to only reach 14C in London on Thursday, with most of the UK seeing the mercury drop below 10C.

It comes after Storm Dave brought snow and strong winds over Easter weekend, causing travel chaos and leaving homes without power as it swept across northern parts of the UK.

Gusts reached 93mph at Capel Curig in North Wales, while winds of 75mph were recorded at Emley Moor in West Yorkshire and St Bees Head in Cumbria, and one of 73mph was recorded at Buchan in Aberdeenshire, the Met Office said.

Some properties in Scotland were left without power following the high winds overnight. Scottish and Southern Electricity Networks (SSEN) fault response teams were out on the network working to reconnect the small number of customers affected, mainly in Skye, Caithness and coastal parts of Aberdeenshire.

Met Office weather forecast

Today:

A chilly, but bright start. Plenty of sunny spells through the day, though cloudier skies at times in the west. A few splashes of rain are possible for Northern Ireland and northwest Scotland. Breezy in the west. Feeling warmer for many.

Tonight:

A fine evening, though turning chilly again under the clear spells overnight, with a patchy frost in the east. A few showers are still possible in the far northwest.

Tuesday:

Most places dry with sunny spells. Cloud and outbreaks of rain moving across Northern Ireland and western Scotland during the afternoon. Breezy in the west. Feeling warm in the sunshine.

Outlook for Wednesday to Friday:

Mostly dry on Wednesday, with spells of warm sunshine. Turning fresher for all from Thursday, with showers or longer spells of rain. Potentially very windy in the northwest come Friday.

Every February 11, the anniversary of the untimely death of my 19-year-old best friend hits me and I feel a heaviness that doesn’t lift until the day’s end.

The day when you lost a loved one, had an accident, or experienced another traumatic event can trigger grief, anger, sadness and anxiety – and also cause physical symptoms, like sickness and insomnia. In more severe cases, people suffering from PTSD may relive experiences in vivid flashbacks or dreams.

Experts call this “anniversary syndrome” or the “anniversary effect,” and every person’s experience is unique. Some 70 percent of U.S. adults say they’ve experienced at least one traumatic event, according to the National Council for Behavioral Health.

“During these times, these feelings and reactions can be strong and often ‘take you back,’” the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention says. The symptoms might begin in the weeks before and intensify as the date nears, the CDC adds. Some may continue for weeks after the anniversary.

But these symptoms don’t last forever and experts have identified several steps people can take to feel relief, both mentally and physically.

open image in gallery Traumatic anniversaries can bring up feelings of grief, anxiety and sadness. Experts say there are steps to help counter these effects ( AFP via Getty Images )

The rhythms of health

Getting the federally-recommended seven hours of sleep a night is important but so is sticking to a schedule. If you don’t keep a sleep routine, it can throw off your circadian rhythm - the body’s way of regulating hormones, digestion and temperature, according to the Cleveland Clinic.

Disrupting that internal clock can worsen the anniversary effect and also increase the likelihood of developing anxiety and depression.

So stick to a sleep schedule. That means going to bed and waking up at the same time, including on weekends, the Mayo Clinic instructs.

Going for a walk in sunlight, within the hour you wake up, helps signal to your brain and body that it’s daytime, says Banner Health nurse practitioner Alexandra Lessem, “setting the circadian clock.”

If you can’t be outside, sitting by an open window with direct sunlight has a similar effect.

A balanced diet packed with fruit and vegetables is crucial for a good night’s sleep. Several foods naturally contain melatonin, such as cherries, pistachios, almonds, eggs and fish, the National Institutes of Health says, and can help make you sleepy.

It’s important to drink plenty of water and move your body every day. As little as 10 minutes of moderate or vigorous activity, such as walking briskly or running, is enough to get more restorative sleep, Benjamin Baird, research assistant professor of psychology at the University of Texas at Austin, said.

Mindful medicine

A few minutes of meditation a day helps with symptoms of anxiety, depression and trauma, and lets people connect with their inner self.

The ancient mind-body practice regulates the sympathetic nervous system, lowers the heart rate and levels of the stress hormone cortisol, the Cleveland Clinic says.

If you are new to meditation, begin with just a minute and build from there. There are a number of styles but some easy places to start include mindfulness meditation, which focuses on the breath, a certain image or feeling, or mantra meditation which has users repeat a certain word or phrase.

Guided meditation - following an expert in person or in one of many online apps - can help beginners tap into the process.

Journaling is a valuable practice for coping with the “anniversary effect.” It is widely used in therapy to help patients process painful feelings - and focus their minds on what they are grateful for or positive experiences.

“It may feel safest to bury painful feelings and avoid confronting them, but acknowledging what happened and how it has impacted you is an important part of healing,” the non-profit Mental Health America says.

open image in gallery Meditation can help to lower heart rate and levels of the stress hormone cortisol. The practice is thousands of years old ( AFP via Getty Images )

Social service

As a difficult date on the calendar approaches, reach out to family and friends.

“There are some folks that, even months before, are nervous about the anniversary,” Laura Murray, a senior scientist in mental health and a clinical psychologist at Johns Hopkins Medicine, said in a statement. “They're thinking about it, trying to figure out how to manage it - we sometimes describe this as spinning.”

Telling others not to bring up a death or traumatic event in the days before an anniversary can help friends or family struggling with trauma to avoid undue stress.

Make plans - even if it’s something small like going to a movie with a loved one or a board game night with friends. “It is important not to isolate yourself. Instead make efforts to be with others,” the National Center for PTSD says.

If you don’t want to confide in friends and family, talk to a trauma therapist. These experts are specifically trained in techniques such as eye movement desensitization and reprocessing therapy. The therapy, first tested in 1989, involves moving your eyes a specific way while you process traumatic memories. It can improve mood without having to talk about negative events, the Cleveland Clinic says.

All in the technique

Mental health experts recommend some tools that can alleviate the anniversary effect.

If you are feeling stressed or stuck thinking about the event, focus on the five senses - sight, smell, touch, sound and taste - to bring you back to the present, the National Alliance on Mental Illness says. This might start with the feel of your clothing, the sound of bird chirping nearby or the smell of food wafting from a restaurant.

“Then notice four of each, then three of each, and so on,” the alliance advises.

Being told to stay positive may make you roll your eyes, but thinking positively can reduce stress, according to Johns Hopkins Medicine. Bring up some of those silly cat videos on your phone - the simple acts of smiling and laughing fight stress by lowering heart rate and blood pressure.

Or pay it forward: send someone a thoughtful card or buy a coffee for a stranger. Making others feel good can make you feel good about yourself.
